study_identification_part.si_4_title: Neurofind: using deep learning to make individualised inferences in brain-based disorders

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The normative models were trained on four publicly available HC datasets: HCP Young Adult (referred to as 'Human Connectome Project' with data release link to HCP Young Adults), HCP Aging, UK Biobank, and IXI. Three additional clinical datasets (AIBL, MCIC, COBRE) were used for exemplar applications. Table S1 shows 7 scanners across training datasets (HCP: N=599; HCP Aging: N=458; Biobank S01: N=1462; Biobank S02: N=349; IXI S01: N=293; IXI S02: N=165; IXI S03: N=36) and 4 scanners across clinical datasets (AIBL: N=122; MCIC S01: N=64; MCIC S02: N=40; MCIC S03: N=52; COBRE: N=86).

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: All four training datasets (HCP-YA, HCP-A, UK Biobank, IXI) contributed healthy controls to a single train set (N=3362) used to develop both the Outlier Detection (AAE) and Brain Age (SVR) normative models, as well as the Neuroharmony scanner harmonisation model. The three clinical datasets (AIBL, MCIC, COBRE) were used solely for exemplar applications to demonstrate the tool, not for model training. For AAE hyperparameter tuning, 75% of the train set was used for training and 25% for validation; the best configuration was then retrained on the entire train set. For SVR, 10-fold cross-validated grid search was used within the train set.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Both models were trained on the same train set of 3362 healthy controls. No separate held-out test set from the HC data is described for either normative model. For the AAE, hyperparameter tuning used a 75/25 internal train/validation split, but the final model was retrained on the full 3362. For the SVR, 10-fold cross-validation was used for hyperparameter selection, then the chosen C was applied to the whole training set. Therefore, overall-phase equals train-phase. The initial sample was 13,918 T1-weighted images; after exclusions (missing data, age outside 20-80, MRIQC quality threshold >0.7, undersampling of UK Biobank, iterative outlier removal), 3362 remained. Per-scanner breakdown from Table S1: HCP=599, HCP Aging=458, Biobank S01=1462, Biobank S02=349, IXI S01=293, IXI S02=165, IXI S03=36.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Both models share the same train set (N=3362), so age statistics are identical. Table 1 reports median=52.0 and a value of 15.2 in brackets. The bracket format in Table 1 is 'median [Q1, Q3]' per the column header, but only a single value (15.2) appears, which likely represents the IQR width rather than separate Q1 and Q3. Therefore Q1 and Q3 cannot be individually determined. Mean and SD are not reported and cannot be reliably computed because per-dataset age distributions are not provided. Min and max are inferred from the inclusion criterion: 'Participants ... younger than 20 and older than 80 years old were excluded', and this is consistent with Fig. 1 showing age range approximately 20-80. Since overall-phase equals train-phase for both models, the values are the same.
